newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Blue-chip firms lift Morocco's bourse.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chip firms lift Morocco's bourse.

text.p: The Casablanca stock exchange closed the week on Friday 4.27 percent higher with blue chip stocks accounting for the bulk of trade during the week, a stockbroker said.
The all-share index closed at 676.47 points from 648.73 points last Friday.
ONA group, the country's largest private holding, closed at 840 dirhams from 824 dirhams, the week before with some 77,512 shares traded on the week.

Societe Nationale d'Investissement, Morocco's second largest conglomerate, which holds diversified stakes in more than 40 firms, closed at 750 dirhams from 720 dirhams from last Friday with 42,735 shares exchanged on the week.
Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur closed at 620 dirhams from 602 dirhams last week with 44,940 shares changing hands.
Leading stock Wafabank traded at 892 dirhams from 870 dirhams last week with 17,753 shares traded on the week.

First tranche of privatisation bonds issued in January last year rose to 1,442 dirhams from 1,310 dirhams on the week after privatisation ministry said that the next flotation would target mining company Societe Metallurgique d'Imiter (SMI) in May.
Banque Nationale pour le Developpement Economique closed at 230 dirhams from 227 dirhams last week.
Steel mill Sonasid closed at 619 dirhams from 576 dirhams last week.
Ciments de L'Oriental closed at 853 dirhams from 760 last week.
Leasing firm Maroc-Leasing, which was listed on the bourse late in February, closed at 551 dirhams from 477 dirhams with 14,201 shares exchanged on the week.
Credit firm Credor, floated in December last year, rose to 912 dirhams from 837 dirhams last week.
Main trade on the over-the-counter market was in 16,540 oil refinery Samir shares followed by 14,000 shares, ABN-AMRO Finance stockbrokers said.
